title: Decompose SLOs by route and model-capacity with staged backoff & load-shedding policy
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Define a granular SLO/SLI framework that is decomposed by API route (chat / completion / embeddings / rerank), model class (small/medium/large / quantized), and customer tier; and pair that with an automated, staged backoff and load-shedding policy that preserves the highest-priority customer traffic while protecting regional capacity and overall platform availability.

Scope: This ticket covers definition, policy, monitoring instrumentation, and a runbook for enforcement. Implementation (runtime controls) will be tracked in follow-up tickets but must adhere to the decision points captured here.

Proposed SLI definitions (per endpoint/model variant):
- Availability SLI: percentage of user requests that return a 2xx final response within model-specific latency window AND without server-side errors (5xx or inference-time internal errors). Counted per-route and per-model-variant.
- Latency SLI: p50/p95/p99 tail latency for token-stream first-byte (TTFB) and final-completion time. Latency thresholds are model-class specific (see thresholds below).
- Success/Quality SLI (optional per experiment): fraction of responses passing a lightweight syntactic sanity check and not flagged by safety/core-eval heuristics; used for model rollouts.

Baseline SLO targets (example — adjustable by product tier and model class):
- Small/fast models (e.g., 7B quantized): Availability 99.99% monthly; p95 latency < 120ms; p99 latency < 300ms.
- Medium models (e.g., 13B): Availability 99.95% monthly; p95 latency < 180ms; p99 latency < 450ms.
- Large models (e.g., 70B float): Availability 99.9% monthly; p95 latency < 500ms; p99 latency < 1500ms.
- Embeddings endpoints measured separately: availability 99.99% and p99 latency < 350ms.

Error budget policy:
- Error budget window: 30-day rolling window per endpoint/model tier.
- Burn rate monitoring: we will compute burn rate aggregated to 1h and 6h windows; alerts fire at sustained burn > 2x (warning) and > 5x (critical) of allowable burn.
- When burn > critical for 1h: trigger automated mitigation tier 1 (priority routing + traffic shaping).
- When burn persists > 3h or exceeds absolute budget: escalate to mitigation tier 2 (regional circuit breakers + model fallback).

Staged mitigation / load-shedding policy: (ordered, non-exclusive)
1) Prefer-affine routing: route traffic to lower-burn regions or dedicated capacity if available for the customer.
2) Graceful degradation via soft-quantization: switch to quantized model variant for best-effort customers/traffic classes.
3) Priority-based request admission: attach priority labels to requests (paid-tier, internal, trial, exploratory). When capacity constrained, deny/queue lowest-priority classes with informative 429+Retry-After and explain in dashboard.
4) Token-level shedding: for long-context jobs, refuse context past a dynamic token budget or truncate non-critical prefixes.
5) Model fallback: degrade to a smaller model variant with documented differences in quality.
6) Regional circuit breaker: open circuit for non-critical routes in affected region if regional availability < threshold for 10m.

Circuit breaker thresholds and behaviour (per region & model class):
- Warning state: regional availability drops below (SLO_target - 0.1%) sustained 5m -> notify oncall and traffic router.
- Throttle state: sustained drop below (SLO_target - 0.5%) for 15m -> reduce concurrency, enforce priority admission, increase queue timeouts.
- Open state: sustained drop below (SLO_target - 1.0%) for 30m or absolute p99 latency > 3x threshold -> open circuit for non-pay-tier routes and trigger regional failover to other regions.
- Circuit breaker must include cooldown/backoff: initial open = 5m, probe interval = 60s with sampled health checks; exponential backoff up to 30m on repeated failures.

Monitoring & alerting:
- Dashboards: per-route & per-model SLI panels, burn-rate, regional availability, priority-class traffic mix.
- Alerts: warn at 1h sustained burn > 2x, critical at 1h > 5x; regional degrade warning/critical thresholds as above. Alerts must include suggested runbook actions and links to affected customer list.

Runbook (high level):
1) Triage: validate metrics (SLO dashboards, traces, infra alerts). Attach links to offending PRs or deployments.
2) Short-term mitigation: enable staged mitigation 1-3 (routing, quantized variants, priority admission).
3) If mitigation insufficient, enable regional circuit breaker and initiate cross-region failover.
4) Post-incident: root-cause analysis, update threshold tuning, adjust model variants and capacity plan, communicate with impacted customers.

Decision points to finalize before implementation:
- Exact latency thresholds per model family (trade-off speed vs quality).
- Priority label schema and how SDK/API surface exposes/request metadata.
- API response semantics for denied/queued requests (429 vs 503; body format).
- How to notify users in-console and via webhook when traffic is shed.
- Mapping from product-tier to minimum allowed fallback model.

Success criteria for this work:
- Documented SLI definitions and SLO targets per route/model in Confluence.
- Automated burn-rate alerts and dashboard panels created.
- A validated simulation that demonstrates prioritization maintains paid-tier availability under a synthetic overload test.
- Runbook and incident playbook reviewed by SRE, runtime, and product teams.

Notes: This ticket intentionally separates policy/spec from runtime implementation. Implementation tickets should reference this key and include concrete kube/runtime changes, request headers for priority, and experiments for fallback quality.
